sovereign_country.strategic_role: 最高信誉财富保护、私人银行合规与楚格州加密谷Web3枢纽

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Security Holographic Cold Foil Printing of Collectible Trading Cards

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (unitary federal codified system; cantonal autonomy in notarial, registry and procedural matters)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Swiss Confederation and the People's Republic of China on the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (BIT, signed 27 January 2009, in force 6 April 2010)
Free Trade Agreement between the EFTA States and the People's Republic of China (signed 21 December 2013, in force 1 July 2015)

Convention between the Swiss Confederation and the United States of America for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (signed 2 October 1996, as amended by the Protocol of 23 September 2018, in force 16 December 2019)
Double Taxation Convention between Switzerland and the People's Republic of China (signed 6 July 1990, as amended by the Protocol of 25 September 2013, in force 27 August 2014)
Convention establishing the European Free Trade Association (EFTA Convention, consolidated text adopted at Vaduz, 21 June 2001)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA, SR 951.0) of 10 October 1997, as amended and in force as of 1 January 2024; FINMA Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance (AMLO-FINMA, SR 951.602) of 11 December 2019; Swiss Code of Obligations (OR, SR 220), Articles 620 et seq., 626, 640, 652h and 697i-697m (incorporated company law, as revised by the Stock Corporation Act of 19 June 2020, in force 1 January 2023); Swiss Commercial Register Ordinance (HRegV, SR 221.411) of 17 October 2007; Swiss Criminal Code (SR 311.0), Articles 305bis and 305ter; Embargo Act (SR 946.201) and SECO sanctions implementing ordinances. There is currently no fully public Swiss UBO register; a Federal Council draft law on the transparency of beneficial owners of legal persons (dated 10 June 2022) is still in parliamentary adoption procedure. Disclosure is made to the cantonal commercial registry only for founding persons at registration, while ongoing UBO information must be reported to financial intermediaries under Article 3 AMLA and obtained upon request by authorities such as the Money Laundering Reporting Office of Switzerland (MROS), criminal prosecutors and tax authorities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney (Vollmacht / procuration) granted by each founding shareholder to the Swiss formation agent and notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent registry authority in the founder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille under the Apostille Convention of 5 October 1961 (accepted for China as of 7 November 2023 and for the United States); Swiss consular legalization at the Embassy or Consulate of Switzerland for non-Convention states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing (registry extract) of each corporate founding shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official commercial register or business registry in the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Swiss consular legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of the identification document (passport or national ID) of each founder, director and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of issuance or residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Swiss consular legalization; alternatively notarization before a Swiss public notary upon original presentation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO declaration and beneficial-ownership self-certification form compliant with Article 3 AMLA
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss or foreign notary public, or the regulated formation fiduciary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille or consular legalization when executed abroad; Swiss notarization is preferred for direct and immediate acceptance

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter or negative PEP clearance certificate issued by the founder's relationship bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed commercial bank in the founder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille or consular legalization; bank-to-bank SWIFT confirmation is accepted by many Swiss banks in lieu of notarized copies

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Founders' declaration and Articles of Association (Statuten) in an official Swiss language (German, French, Italian or Romansh)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public notary (öffentlicher Notar / notaire) of the canton of the registered office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarization only; no apostille or consular legalization is required because the public deed is registered ex officio with the cantonal Commercial Register

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all founders, directors, authorized signatories and UBOs, performed by the regulated formation fiduciary before signature of the public deed. Screening must cover: (i) the Swiss SECO sanctions database (SESAM) implementing UN Security Council embargoes and autonomously adopted Swiss measures under the Embargo Act (SR 946.201); (ii) the OFAC SDN list, which is contractually required by US correspondent banks for USD settlement through Stripe and Authorize_Net; (iii) the consolidated UN Security Council sanctions lists; (iv) FATF high-risk jurisdiction and public statement lists; and (v) domestic and foreign PEP registers covering governmental, judicial, military and state-owned enterprise officials pursuant to FATF Recommendation 12 and Article 3 AMLA. For the designated Low_Risk_Standard commercial model, simplified due diligence under Article 12 AMLO-FINMA may apply, but the screening result, risk rating and client-file documentation must be retained by the fiduciary and made available to the financial intermediary opening the corporate bank account.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: ZEFIX - Zentraler Firmenindex (Swiss Central Business Name Index) operated by the Federal Commercial Registry Office (Eidgenössisches Amt für das Handelsregister, EAHR), publicly searchable at www.zefix.ch; formal name-application filings are submitted to the cantonal Commercial Registry Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the canton of the registered office.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Articles 950-951 of the Swiss Code of Obligations and Articles 7-10 HRegV, a corporate name must be true (Wahrheit), clearly distinguishable from all existing registry and trademark names, and free of misleading references to public authorities, industries or regulated activities. The name must be written in an official Swiss language (German, French, Italian or Romansh) using Latin script; a foreign-language or romanized name, e.g., English or transliterated Chinese (pinyin), is admissible for an internationally active business provided it is not misleading. The full legal name must contain the mandatory legal-form suffix 'Aktiengesellschaft' or the abbreviation 'AG' (French: 'SA').
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms implying public-law character or connection with Swiss federal or cantonal authorities: 'Schweiz', 'Eidgenossenschaft', 'Bund', 'Swiss', 'national', and official coats of arms or heraldic emblems (Article 33 HRegV; Federal Act on the Protection of the Swiss Coat of Arms)
'Bank', 'bancaire', 'Sparkasse', 'deposit business' — requires a FINMA banking license under the Swiss Banking Act of 8 November 1934
'Insurance', 'Versicherung', 'reinsurance' — requires a FINMA or private-insurance supervisory license
'Securities dealer', 'Effektenhändler', 'stock exchange', 'investment fund' — requires a FINMA license under the Swiss Financial Institutions Act (FINIG) or CISA
'Trust', 'Fiduciary', 'Treuhand' — admissible only upon proof of AMLA registration as an authorized fiduciary; otherwise considered misleading
'Audit', 'Revision', 'Wirtschaftsprüfung' — reserved for companies licensed under Article 906 CO
'Law firm', 'Rechtsanwalt', 'Notariat', 'advocacy' — restricted by the Swiss Federal Lawyers Act and cantonal notarial laws
Names containing profanity, incitement, misstatements of business purpose, geographic names other than the exact registered seat, or references infringing third-party trademark rights

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (CO), Arts. 620–659 (Aktiengesellschaft); CO Art. 629 (minimum capital), Art. 632 (paid-up capital), Art. 635 (notarized deed), Art. 640 (commercial register application), Art. 716a (non-delegable board duties), Art. 718 (signature authority); Swiss Commercial Register Ordinance (HRegV, SR 221.411); Swiss Civil Code Arts. 52–59 (legal personality).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug), supervised by the Swiss Federal Office for the Justice, with public search via the Central Business Name Index (ZEFIX).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association (Statuten) together with the Declaration for Entry in the Commercial Register (Anmeldung zur Eintragung ins Handelsregister) under CO Art. 640.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum nominal share capital is CHF 100,000 (approx. USD 112,000). At least CHF 50,000 (approx. USD 56,000) must be fully paid up in cash before registration; the deposited amount must be held in a blocked escrow account (Sperrkonto) at a Swiss-regulated bank and a bank blockage confirmation must be filed with the Commercial Register. Funds are released only after registration. In-kind contributions (Sacheinlage) require full payment of the corresponding shares and a statutory audit report in lieu of cash deposit.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION — adopted by the Board of Directors of [Company Name] AG on [Date]. RESOLVED: (1) that the Articles of Association were adopted and that all 1,000 registered shares with a nominal value of CHF 100 each were subscribed in full; (2) that the bank blockage confirmation issued by [Bank Name] evidences the paid-up capital of CHF 50,000 credited to the blocked account; (3) that the registered office is established at [Street Address], [Postal Code] [City], Canton Zug, Switzerland; (4) that [Name] is appointed Chairperson of the Board, [Name] appointed Secretary, and [Name] appointed Managing Director with sole signature authority; and (5) that these officers are authorized to execute and file the Commercial Register application and all ancillary declarations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Business Name Index (ZEFIX) and Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search ZEFIX to verify that the proposed corporate name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name under CO Arts. 951–954. Submit a preliminary name clearance and reservation request directly to the Zug Commercial Register Office, indicating the intended legal form 'AG' and the business purpose clause covering security holographic printing, cold foil printing and publishing of collectible trading cards. The reservation is recorded in the provisional register and secures the name for incorporation.
required_dossiers: Founder's valid passport or national identity document
Proposed company name and at least one alternative
Draft business purpose clause per HRegV Art. 12
Founders' home-canton declaration and contact details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry objects to the name due to identity or confusion, amend the name with a disambiguating element (e.g., a territorial or industry descriptor) or obtain a written consent letter from the owner of the conflicting name. A rejected reservation may be appealed to the Cantonal Commercial Register Supervisory Authority within 10 days; private trademark oppositions are settled by consent or cancellation of the reservation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Canton of Zug (Notariat des Kantons Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founders must appear physically before the notary. The notary reads and authenticates the Deed of Incorporation and the Articles of Association, verifies the identity and legal capacity of each subscriber, and ensures the articles contain all mandatory elements of CO Art. 626: corporate name, registered office, purpose, share capital, nominal value and number of shares, board representation rules, and publication organ (Swiss Official Commercial Gazette). The notary issues a certified copy for subsequent filing.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association per CO Arts. 626 and 627
Name reservation certificate from step 1
Founders' valid passport or identity card
Beneficial owner declaration and AML identification form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies drafting or legal deficiencies, a correction addendum (Berichtigungsprotokoll) is prepared and re-signed by all founders; substantive defects require reconvening the founding meeting and a fresh notarization. Civil liability of the notary applies for erroneous certification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Capital Account and Deposit of Paid-Up Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss-regulated commercial bank (e.g., Zuger Kantonalbank or another FINMA-licensed bank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a bank account in the name of the company 'in formation' and deposit the required paid-up capital of at least CHF 50,000 from each subscriber in accordance with CO Art. 632. The bank places an irrevocable blocking note on the funds and issues a written blockage confirmation (Sperrkonto-Bestätigung) addressed to the Commercial Register Office. The confirmation must identify the company, the depositors, the amount, and the bank's undertaking to release funds only upon registration.
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation and Articles of Association
AML/KYC forms (Form A and Form B declarations)
Identity documents of all persons with signing power
Proof of source of funds for each capital subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the deposit for AML, FATCA/CRS or source-of-funds concerns, provide bank statements and a formal asset-origin declaration. If the bank refuses, select an alternative FINMA-licensed bank; the Commercial Register accepts a blockage confirmation from any Swiss-regulated bank. Persisting refusal may be escalated through the Swiss Banking Ombudsman.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Register Application, Examination and Publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the signed registration application electronically or in paper via the Zug registry portal. The application must annex the notarized deed and articles, the bank blockage confirmation, board signature specimen cards, the directors' and (if required) auditors' consent declarations, and a declaration that no grounds for disqualification exist. Upon positive examination the registry assigns the UID company identification number and publishes the formation in the Swiss Official Commercial Gazette (SHAB), which completes incorporation and grants legal personality.
required_dossiers: Registration application form per HRegV Art. 48
Notarized deed of incorporation and Articles of Association
Bank blockage confirmation (Sperrkonto-Bestätigung)
Signature specimen cards (Unterzeichnete Musterkarten)
Directors', secretary's and auditor's written consents
Declaration on absence of bankruptcy or disqualifying criminal convictions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A deficiency notice (Mängelliste) must be cured by supplementary filings within the registry deadline, normally 20 days. If the application is rejected, an appeal lies to the Cantonal Economic Department of Zug and thereafter to the Swiss Federal Supreme Court. Third-party objections to the registration are litigated before the Zug Commercial Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) for UID and VAT; Cantonal AHV Compensation Office; SUVA; Municipality of Zug for business tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the entry is published, the UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) is automatically issued by ESTV. Register the company as an employer with the AHV Compensation Office and with SUVA for accident insurance. Submit the VAT registration questionnaire to ESTV if worldwide turnover reaches or exceeds CHF 100,000, or apply voluntarily for immediate VAT liability (Art. 10 Swiss VAT Act). Inform the municipal tax office of the business location and complete the local business permit procedure.
required_dossiers: Commercial register excerpt confirming the entry
Notarized Articles of Association
Employer registration form for AHV and SUVA
ESTV VAT registration questionnaire
Shareholders' and beneficial owner declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late VAT or social insurance registration may trigger default interest and administrative fines; file an overdue registration request with credible justification and, where the delay is without fault, the sanction is generally waived by ESTV or the compensation office. UID issuance delays are cured by request to ESTV.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No sectoral industrial concession is required in Switzerland for non-monetary printing and foil-stamping of collectible trading cards; operational oversight is exercised by the Canton of Zug Office of Economics and Labour (Amt für Wirtschaft und Arbeit, AWA) for workplace conditions and by the Canton of Zug Environmental Protection Office (Amt für Umweltschutz Zug) for emissions and waste permits.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — the activity does not constitute 'security printing' under the Swiss Federal Act on Currency and Payment Instruments (Bundesgesetz über die Währung und Zahlungsmittel); no dead or operating license must be obtained from the federal or cantonal authorities. The production site requires only a municipal building and land-use permit (Baubewilligung) adopted by the building department of the Municipality of Zug.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Canton of Zug Environmental Protection Office (Amt für Umweltschutz des Kantons Zug) with binding technical standards issued by the Swiss Federal Office for the Environment (BAFU/FOEN)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C — registration with minimal intervention; no full environmental impact assessment (EIA) is required under the Swiss EIA Ordinance (VPVU, SR 814.011) for foil printing and cold-foil stamping lines below 200 tonnes of organic solvents consumed annually; a full EIA Report becomes mandatory if the facility exceeds this solvent-throughput threshold or is integrated with paper coating operations, in which case classification rises to Category A/B.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Air emissions: compliance with the Swiss Clean Air Ordinance (LRV, SR 814.318.142.1), Annex 2 — solvent-laden exhaust from printing and foil processes must not exceed 20 g VOC per square metre of printed substrate, and waste-gas concentrations are capped at 20 mg/m³ for non-methane VOCs unless equipped with an abatement system; Wastewater: compliance with the Swiss Water Protection Ordinance (GSchV, SR 814.201) — discharges from equipment cleaning and cooling circuits must contain no chlorinated hydrocarbons, total mineral-oil hydrocarbons ≤ 20 mg/l, pH 6.5–9.5, and be routed through an oil separator before the public sewer; Solid waste: holographic foil offcuts and stamping residue are classified as non-hazardous production waste and must be surrendered to a canton-approved recycling or incineration plant with annual waste-balance reporting; VOC incentivisation tax (Lenkungsabgabe) registration is effected with BAFU/ESTV based on solvent purchases.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification: final fire-police acceptance (feuerpolizeiliche Abnahme) issued by the Zug Cantonal Fire Insurance (Gebäudeversicherung Zug) after inspection of emergency exits, fire zones and extinguishing systems. Structural load clearance: municipal building inspector's certificate confirming floor-load calculations for heavy foil-stamping presses (design floor load not below 5 kN/m²). Occupational clearance: SUVA worksite inspection for machine guarding, noise emission, ventilation of solvent areas and emergency-stop installations, together with the employer's certificate of accident-insurance coverage prerequisite for the start of production.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung – ESTV / Administration Fédérale des Contributions – AFC / Amministrazione Federale delle Contribuzioni – AVC), official portal: www.estv.admin.ch; electronic filing via Swiss eTax and ePortal for VAT (www.estv.admin.ch/mwst) and corporate income tax at cantonal level.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity not established in Switzerland performing taxable supplies in Switzerland must register with ESTV for a Swiss VAT number and Company Identification Number (UID). The online registration (via ESTV eServices) requires: foreign certificate of incorporation, proof of the foreign business address, evidence of taxable supplies in Switzerland, name of a Swiss VAT representative if no Swiss seat/branch, and designation of payment rails. The UID and VAT number are issued within approximately 5–10 business days; effective VAT liability commences from the date of taxable business activity in Switzerland.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss law has no pass-through or check-the-box election. Available elective statutory grouping mechanisms include Swiss VAT group taxation under Art. 12 MWSTG for economically, financially and organisationally integrated entities, and tax consolidation at the federal/cantonal level under Art. 18 Federal Corporate Income Tax Act (DBG) and Art. 2 Swiss Harmonised Tax Act (SHIG) for a group of resident subsidiaries. Hybrid mismatch elections are unavailable; Swiss law aligns with OECD BEPS recommendations requiring the relevant entity's tax treatment to follow its local legal classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Mehrwertsteuer / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée / Imposta sul valore aggiunto)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 250,000 in annual turnover from taxable supplies (excluding exempt supplies) for suppliers with Swiss seat/place of business; non-established suppliers are subject to registration without a de minimis threshold where they carry on a taxable activity in Switzerland and their B2C supplies are not covered by the Swiss recipient's reverse-charge mechanism; a non-resident supplier may elect to register voluntarily for VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not mandate a real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping system. VAT-compliant invoices must be issued in accordance with Art. 26 MWSTG; electronic invoices are legally recognized. The Swiss QR-bill (QR-Rechnung) is the standardized payment slip format commonly used but is not an indirect-tax clearance instrument. VAT returns and periodic statements are filed electronically via ESTV eTax; invoices and export proof must be retained for 10 years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods out of Swiss customs territory to a foreign country are zero-rated under Art. 23 MWSTG where the supplier or a third party proves that the goods have been physically exported and the destination is a foreign customs territory. Export-related direct services, including freight, dispatch, and services dealt with directly on exported goods, are also zero-rated. For goods sold by a Swiss AG to a foreign buyer under CIF/FOB terms with delivery outside Switzerland, the zero rate applies upon possession of the fully executed Swiss export declaration and foreign import evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Zollinhaltsdeklaration / Swiss electronic customs declaration)
Transport document (Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR Convention consignment note)
Commercial invoice with explicit export VAT zero-rating clause
Foreign customs entry or import customs declaration evidencing arrival in destination country
Bank settlement statement / SWIFT MT103 evidencing payment of the cross-border consideration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Swiss Federal Tax Administration and cantonal tax authorities may retroactively audit export zero-rating documentation within statutory limitation periods. Missing, incomplete, or found-false export proof triggers retrospective VAT assessment at the standard 7.7% rate plus default interest. Abuse or intentional fraudulent invocation of export zero-rating constitutes tax evasion under Art. 96 MWSTG, subject to a fine up to the amount of tax evaded, confiscation, and in aggravating organised cases criminal penalties under Art. 98 below; repayment of wrongly credited input VAT is enforced with penal interest and administrative surcharge.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB / Schweizerische Nationalbank), acting as sole monetary authority for the Swiss franc (CHF), in coordination with the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA), which supervises banks, securities dealers, and AML/CFT compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full and unrestricted currency convertibility on both current and capital accounts. No exchange-control laws, no prior-approval requirements, and no licensing barriers apply to FX transactions or profit remittance by a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft (AG). Dividend distributions are subject to a 35% Swiss anticipatory withholding tax, which may be reduced or refunded under applicable double-taxation treaties, whereas capital repayment and current-account trade settlements are free of withholding tax. The CHF is classified as a freely usable and fully convertible currency by the IMF; no material profit-repatriation hurdles exist beyond standard corporate income tax and withholding tax compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Switzerland imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio or repatriation deadline for export receipts. The AG may retain export proceeds in any convertible currency, hold foreign-currency accounts with licensed Swiss banks, and freely time conversion to CHF. The only applicable obligation is indirect: monetary financial institutions report Swiss balance-of-payments statistics to the SNB under the National Bank Ordinance; the exporting AG itself carries no filing duty except standard bookkeeping and tax disclosure.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Trade Finance Facility

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM-HIGH with material legal constraints. A Swiss AG may lawfully open payment accounts with FINMA-licensed fintech banks or FINMA-licensed fintech licensees (e.g., Swissquote-type entities operating under Art. 1b Swiss Banking Act), as well as with EEA or UK electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as Wise, Airwallex, or MultiPass. However, foreign EMIs are not Swiss banks: they do not participate in SIC (Swiss Interbank Clearing), do not hold a Swiss banking license, do not benefit from the Swiss depositor-protection privilege (Art. 37b Banking Act), and cannot hold Swiss-resident client funds without FINMA authorization. Consequently, an offshore EMI should be used strictly as a pass-through settlement rail for cross-border receivables and payables, never as the primary CHF treasury hub. Domestic FINMA-regulated fintechs offer fully digital onboarding but generally cap deposits at CHF 100 million per client and charge premium per-transaction fees.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under FINMA Circular 2016/07, remote onboarding through certified video identification combined with a qualified electronic signature is legally permitted, and unconditional physical presence is not a statutory mandate. In practice, tier-1 Swiss commercial banks require at least one authorized director, preferably the Swiss-resident signatory, to attend a physical KYC interview for the initial relationship, and they reserve discretion to demand in-person verification for foreign UBOs, early-stage entities, and industries involving high-value collectibles. The optimal protocol: a Swiss resident director opens the account in person with the corporate seal and notarized board resolution; non-resident co-directors complete remote video identification with apostilled passport copies, Certified Certificate of Incorporation, and evidentiary source-of-funds documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Early-stage AG without audited financial statements, minimal operating history, and statutory share capital of CHF 100,000 paid in from a foreign jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Handelsregister (Commercial Register) excerpt, notarized Articles of Association, board resolution authorizing account opening, bank reference from the paying bank, notarized share-subscription deeds, source-of-wealth declarations for each shareholder, and a 24-month cash-flow forecast referencing the Stripe/Authorize.Net payment rails.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Collectible-trading-card manufacturing flagged under money-laundering typologies (speculative high-value tangible assets, secondary-market resale, potential NFT-adjacent digital wrappers)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Documented AML risk assessment assigning Low_Risk_Standard classification, internal transaction-monitoring procedures, KYC files on distributors and marketplace counterparties, inventory provenance and retention policy, sample invoices with tariff classification ISIC 3240 / NAICS 323111, and a compliance manual covering sanctions screening and suspicious-transaction reporting to MROS (Swiss Money Laundering Reporting Office).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ambiguous source of funds for the CHF 100,000 minimum capital and any shareholder loans, particularly when funds originate from foreign corporate shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank-to-bank SWIFT records showing the complete funds path, audited or notarized financial statements of the shareholder, organizational chart revealing the ultimate beneficial owner, signed declaration of source of funds, corporate registry excerpts from the shareholder's jurisdiction, and tax residence certificates to exclude round-tripping.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payment flows toward FATF grey-list or sanctions-implicated jurisdictions in the printing-supply or wholesale-distribution chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due diligence file per counterparty, executed export/import contracts with Incoterms, bills of lading and customs declarations, bank-confirmed letters of credit for high-ticket shipments, jurisdiction risk-rating matrix, and a restricted-country filter configured to automatically block prohibited corridors.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Share capital injection must be wired via SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's bank to the AG's designated CHF provisional capital account (Sperrkonto) at a licensed Swiss bank. The bank issues a paid-up capital confirmation (Sperrkonto-Bestätigung) for notarization under Art. 632 and 633 of the Swiss Code of Obligations. Purpose codes must align with the Swiss Payment Standards and SNB balance-of-payments statistical classification: the transfer is categorized as 'equity capital injection / direct investment' rather than trade receivables. Verification bundle: notarized deed of subscription, bank confirmation of blocked funds, board minutes approving the capital increase, and final Commercial Register entry for the paid-in capital. Shareholder loans are permissible and may be denominated in foreign currency; they must be evidenced by formal loan agreements with arm's-length interest rates to avoid recharacterization as hidden equity and to prevent exposure to Swiss anticipatory tax, which applies to distributions but not to genuine loan servicing.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (1) SIC (Swiss Interbank Clearing) for domestic CHF and SEPA EUR payments; (2) SWIFT MT103 for international cross-border wires, with mandatory structured narrative referencing invoice number, Incoterms, and commodity description for collectible trading cards; (3) irrevocable and confirmed commercial Letters of Credit opened by UBS AG or ZKB trade-finance desks for wholesale shipments exceeding defined risk thresholds; (4) documentary collections for mid-tier distributor purchases; and (5) third-party card-acquiring rails (Stripe, Authorize.Net) for retail e-commerce settlement, which are treated as pass-through payment collection and swept daily to the Swiss treasury account. All disbursements must satisfy record-keeping requirements of the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance (AMLO) and fall within bank-reported SNB balance-of-payments thresholds; no corporate-level filing is triggered.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CHF/USD and CHF/EUR FX forward contracts executed with FINMA-regulated Swiss banks or their licensed international branches
FX swaps (overnight and term) for temporary conversion of CHF into settlement currencies for trade payments
Cross-currency swaps (XCCY) for medium-term financing and balance-sheet hedging under an ISDA master agreement with CSA collateral
European-style vanilla over-the-counter currency options (call/put) with FINMA-regulated counterparties for optionality on large export receipts
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) restricted to illiquid emerging-market currencies where deliverability is unavailable; unnecessary for CHF, which is fully convertible and freely deliverable

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Corporate Income Tax Return (Federal Direct Tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) acting through the Cantonal Tax Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 March of the following fiscal year; automatic extension to 30 September upon application; fiscal year is the calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest of 4.75% p.a.; late-filing penalty up to CHF 10,000 (approx. USD 11,500); willful evasion triggers criminal fine up to 2× recalculated tax; persistent non-filing can lead to judicial dissolution and administrative strike-off from the Swiss Commercial Register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Cantonal Income and Capital Tax Return (Assessment Declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration (canton of registered office, e.g., Zug, Zurich, or Geneva)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 March of the following calendar year; extension to 30 September upon justified request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest of 4.75% p.a.; penalty up to 3× the amount of concealed cantonal tax; administrative enforcement and strike-off risk after repeated non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Swiss VAT Return and Annual VAT Settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV), VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after each quarterly VAT period; final annual settlement due no later than 31 March of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default tax of 5% of the outstanding VAT amount if paid late; disciplinary fine up to CHF 10,000; criminal evasion penalty up to 2× VAT due and potential imprisonment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Social Insurance Wage Declaration and Contributions (AHV/ALV/NBUV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Compensation Office (AHV-Ausgleichskasse) appointed for the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 January following the wage-earning calendar year; contributions due on same statutory date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Contribution arrears interest; penalty for omission or inaccurate declaration up to 3× underpaid contributions; personal liability of directors under Art. 52 (AHVG) for unpaid employer contributions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary mandatory audit required when any two of three criteria are exceeded for two consecutive fiscal years: balance sheet total CHF 20 million, turnover CHF 40 million, and 250 full-time employees on annual average. Limited audit (review) is compulsory when any two of three criteria are exceeded: balance sheet total CHF 10 million, turnover CHF 20 million, and 50 full-time employees, unless shareholders holding a qualified majority expressly opt for a simplified review or audit exemption in a legally permitted micro-AG structure.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR 957-962) financial reporting requirements; optional application of Swiss GAAP FER or IFRS; consolidated statutory accounts for listed groups must apply Swiss GAAP FER, IFRS, or recognized equivalent.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Switzerland maintains no public UBO register. Swiss AGs must keep an internal Aktienregister (register of shareholders) with accurate beneficial ownership documentation. Upon each share transfer or ownership change, the board of directors must update the share register and minutes. An annual internal confirmation of the register’s accuracy is recommended; Swiss financial intermediaries and tax authorities may request UBO documentation during audits, and the general meeting must approve the annual financial statements and confirm proper maintenance of statutory books.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CHF 300 – CHF 700 (approx. USD 350 – 800) per annum for Swiss registered office and corporate agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: CHF 4,000 – CHF 12,000 (approx. USD 4,500 – 13,500) for limited audit/review; ordinary audit CHF 20,000 and above in typical market ranges

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal direct tax 8.5% on profit after tax (7.83% on pre-tax profit) plus cantonal and municipal profit tax; combined effective Zug rate for an AG approximately 11.9%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Switzerland grants no general statutory tax holidays; available preferential deductions under the 2020 tax reform (STAF/OA17): patent box exempting 90% of qualifying innovation income from cantonal tax, R&D super-deduction of up to 150% of qualifying research and development personnel cost per canton, notional interest deduction (NID) on excess equity, and the participation relief (Beteiligungsabzug) eliminating profit tax on qualifying dividends and capital gains from investments of at least 10%

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Combined federal and cantonal corporate income tax return for legal persons (Steuererklärung juristische Personen; Zug Form A/B 2024); electronic filing through the cantonal portal e-Steuererklärung Zug and federal ESTV modules (DTS federal direct tax and Verrechnungssteuer) at estv.admin.ch
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, aligned to the shareholder-approved statutory financial statements; interim profit tax instalments are payable quarterly based on the most recent assessment
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Statutory deadline within six months after fiscal year-end (Art. 125 DBG); for calendar-year taxpayers the cantonal practice prescribes 31 March with a commonly granted extension to 30 September, and further extension on documented request

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total assets per the statutory balance sheet (Swiss Code of Obligations, Swiss GAAP FER or IFRS if applied)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the AG is nominally Swiss but tax-resident abroad under the DTA, report only the Swiss permanent establishment (Betriebsstätte) balance sheet; otherwise report worldwide assets

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit for the fiscal year before tax, as presented in the audited income statement
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the profit attributable to the Swiss activity as evidenced by Swiss GAAP accounts; DTA-resident foreign managers may not offset foreign head-office losses

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible items and hidden profit distributions to be added back to the accounting profit: non-arm's length management fees, royalties, interest and inventory pricing adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign shareholders must expect recharacterisation of undervalued services or intra-group royalties as constructive dividends subject to 35% Swiss withholding tax

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of commercially carried loss carryforwards, limited to the prior seven tax years and to the same activity with unchanged ownership and bookkeeping requirements
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident acquirers of the AG must verify the continuation of economic identity to preserve any loss carryforward inventory

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation schedules for the participation relief on qualifying dividend income and for the cantonal patent box (90% exemption) on proceeds of qualifying security and trading-card printing IP
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign recipients of dividends must attach the group participation list and update the ESTV documentary evidence to support a reduced withholding rate

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim for refund or credit of the 35% Swiss anticipatory tax withheld on Swiss-source income of the AG
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only the AG as the Swiss resident taxpayer may claim the refund; foreign shareholders independently claim their DTA recovery under the treaty protocol

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a procedural fine (Ordnungsbusse) of up to CHF 10,000 per Art. 174 DBG, default assessment at the tax administration's discretion with a surcharge of up to 5% of assessed tax, and arrears interest of 4.5% p.a. on the federal portion plus cantonal late-payment interest; repeated non-compliance escalates to criminal tax proceedings before the cantonal tax court

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss anticipatory tax (Verrechnungssteuer) withheld at source on any distribution; the AG must gross up the dividend so that the recipient bears the tax and the cash cost to the AG equals the net declared dividend
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Relief is obtained either in the simplified relief-at-source procedure or by refund: for an EU parent company holding at least 10% of the share capital for at least 12 months, the Swiss-EU agreement of 2015 permits relief at source on Form 823/824 lodged with ESTV; for all other treaty partners, the recipient must submit a refund claim Form 822/823 to ESTV within three years (Art. 32 VStG) attaching a current Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) and beneficial-ownership statement; ESTV routinely requests substance evidence for treaty-shopping screening; the Swiss payor remains strictly liable for unpaid 35% WHT if documentation is deficient
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: no statutory or treaty withholding tax on licence and IP fees (0%) paid to non-residents, except where the licence is economically connected to a Swiss permanent establishment. Interest: 0% WHT on ordinary commercial and bank debt interest; 35% statutory WHT applies to interest on bonds and money-market instruments issued by a Swiss resident (Art. 4 VStG), reducible under DTA provisions to treaty ceilings of 5-10%

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory local-file or master-file thresholds exist in Swiss law; a Country-by-Country Report is mandatory for group consolidated revenue of at least CHF 900,000,000. Under the Federal Tax Administration's transfer pricing guidance (Wegleitung 2023), taxpayers must prepare and present on request contemporaneous arm's-length documentation for all material cross-border controlled transactions, commonly including the ten largest transaction flows, intercompany agreements, comparability analyses and financial benchmarking studies
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland has no dedicated Economic Substance Regulation in the Gulf sense, but equivalent anti-abuse substance principles apply through Art. 50 DBG (place of effective management and administration), Art. 57 DBG (substance over form) and the DTA beneficial-ownership test; a collectible-trading-card AG must maintain operational substance in Switzerland — physical printing and lamination equipment, technical staff for holographic cold-foil processes, decisive board meetings, local bank accounts, and business premises — otherwise the tax authorities may disregard the legal form, attribute the income to the effective managers, or deny treaty benefits, triggering the full 35% anticipatory tax, restitution and criminal fines

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilful submission of false or incomplete Swiss tax returns, concealment of Swiss-source trading-card printing revenue, fictitious royalty outflows, or use of forged supplier invoices for holographic foil materials
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of up to the full amount of the evaded tax per Art. 175/176 DBG; aggravated evasion (Art. 177 DBG) carries imprisonment of up to three years and a fine of up to CHF 30,000, compounded by confiscation of the evaded amount and arrears interest of 4.5% p.a.; the assessment limitation period extends for cases involving documentary forgery
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors signing inaccurate filings incur co-perpetrator liability: imprisonment up to three years, personal fines, civil damages under Art. 754 CO toward creditors, and the claim of the cantonal tax administration against the board in bankruptcy proceedings (Verantwortlichkeitsklage)

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Late or Non-Filing and Procedural Violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to submit the cantonal/federal return by the statutory deadline, incomplete Bogen schedules, refusal to produce transfer-pricing documentation, or obstruction of the fiscal verification process
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Procedural fines up to CHF 10,000 per Art. 174 DBG, discretionary default assessment with a surcharge of up to 5% of the assessed tax, loss of loss-carryforward claims and of participation relief, and cantonal late-payment penalties; a repeated default is prosecuted as procedural criminal offence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Board members are personally liable for the procedural fines and for the company's tax debt where they wilfully or negligently caused the default; Swiss enforcement authorities may additionally impose travel restrictions (Ausreisesperre) on controlling directors for outstanding tax debts

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing and Hidden Profit Distributions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-arm's-length intercompany charges, e.g., inflated royalty for card-branding IP, off-market lending to a foreign shareholder, or sale of security-holographic printed cards to a related distributor at below-market prices
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Upward tax adjustment to the arm's-length result per Art. 58 DBG; recharacterisation as a constructive dividend subject to 35% anticipatory tax; the underpaid tax is recovered with 4.5% p.a. interest and possible 5% default surcharge
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved the non-arm's-length terms are liable to the company for the unpaid withholding tax under the knowledge attribution rules, and the 35% WHT claim can be asserted against the signatory directors personally where the AG becomes insolvent

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML, Shell Company and Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Use of the Swiss AG as a letterbox conduit for collectible-card royalty flows, failure to complete the Swiss beneficial-ownership transparency register, unexplained cash settlement of card sales, or routing payments through high-risk jurisdictions without local substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering under Art. 305bis of the Swiss Criminal Code is punishable by imprisonment of up to three years, or up to five years in qualified cases; the enterprise may additionally be sanctioned with a fine of up to CHF 5,000,000 per Art. 102 StGB, and all illicit proceeds are subject to confiscation; tax authorities will deny treaty benefits and reverse any DTA withholding relief with interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face imprisonment of up to five years, disqualification as board members of Swiss companies, extended confiscation orders, extradition exposure on mutual legal assistance, and personal civil liability to the defrauded co-shareholders and creditors
